Pauses the widget monitor. While paused, watched widgets are not loaded in the background and \'Widget Updated\' events do not fire. The list of watched widgets is kept, so resuming picks them all up again.
Keeps the CPU awake so widget changes are noticed while the screen is off and the device is in Doze. Costs noticeably more battery - a task can switch it on only for the hours you actually need it.

Add a \'Widget Updated\' event in Tasker (Profile → Event → Plugin → WidgetRelay). Its widget then appears here and is kept loaded in the background.
The widgets below are not loaded and \'Widget Updated\' events will not fire until you resume.
Loading the widgets in the background. If this doesn’t change within a few seconds, check the permissions below.
They are loaded invisibly in the background, so Tasker fires as soon as their contents change.
%1$d widget could not be loaded - see the reason below it.
%1$d widgets could not be loaded - see the reason below each one.
Without these, widgets stay empty or stop being watched.
A widget only loads its contents once it sits in a real window. WidgetRelay gives it an invisible one - without this, every widget reads back empty.
The background monitor has to show an ongoing notification. Android only lets it run while that notification can be posted.
Battery optimisation freezes the monitor after a while, so widget changes go unnoticed. Only needed for the \'Widget Updated\' event.
One entry per \'Widget Updated\' event. Tasker doesn’t report a deleted event, so remove entries you no longer need by hand.

Tasker doesn’t tell when a \'Widget Updated\' event is deleted, so this is the only way to stop watching a widget. If you still have that event in Tasker, it will stop firing once this is removed - you can re-add it by opening that event\'s configuration again.
Catches changes while the screen is off and the device is in Doze. Costs noticeably more battery - leave off unless you miss updates overnight.
Starts as soon as monitoring runs and the permissions above are granted.
